keyA.notes: Markers: p.196 ends with bayt 4 complete and its gloss 4 complete, with no footnotes. p.197 starts with bayt 5 and has no '+' and no (تابع). pp.198-200 each also start with a new bayt. Layout: the poem is set stacked in one heavier font, so no ** is used in the verse. Each bayt is one ':::شعر' line. Each page's glosses form a ':::مفردات' block, one line per numbered gloss item. On p.200, gloss 21 is printed with an early line break after «من», but it is one item. Variant notes (pp.198, 199) are ':::حواشي' blocks. Each page prints its two footnotes on one line, written here as two lines. p.200 has no footnotes. The validate.py warnings on pp.198/199 come from the footnote refs sitting inside the poetry fence, which the validator does not count. They are expected. Dagger alif: the gloss font draws a small vertical alif in the bowl of final ى (القذىٰ، أضحىٰ، الضحىٰ، الأذىٰ، عَلَىٰ، حتىٰ، إلىٰ، الذِّفَرىٰ، يرىٰ، تعالىٰ، تَعْرَىٰ، تَضْحَىٰ، مثنىٰ). Following the keyA precedent (b02/b17), it is written ىٰ (U+0649 U+0670). The verse font draws final ى plain (القَذَى، أَضْحَى، عَلَى، الذِّفْرَى), so those are written plain. Overlapping marks (verified by measuring connected components at 1500 dpi): in the initial lam-mim ligature of this verse font, the mim's mark is placed above the lam stem, at the same spot as the lam's own mark. (a) In «الْمَاءَ» (p.198 b.10) and «الْمَراسِيلُ» (p.199 b.14), the single mark above the lam looks like a damma at normal zoom. It is in fact a sukun and a fatha drawn over each other: area 1895 px, versus 1390 for a sukun, 1005 for a fatha and 2110 for a damma, and the shape is a closed loop crossed by a fatha stroke. It is therefore written sukun on the lam and fatha on the mim. Compare المَتْنَيْنِ on p.200, where a plain fatha (the mim's) sits in the same place over the lam. (b) In «خَالُهَا» (p.200 b.21), the mark above the lam-ha ligature is a damma with a fatha merged into it: area 2421 px, with a fatha tip visible. So the ha's fatha also anchors above the lam stem. (c) In «لَهَا» (p.198 b.12), only one fatha is visible above the lam stem. Its area is 1044 px, against 1001-1012 for every single fatha on the page and 1007 for the lone lam fatha of «لَهِقٍ». This means two nearly coincident fathas, so it is written لَهَا. Without that measurement, an eye reading would see a single fatha (لَها or لهَا). Line-crossing marks: several marks hang between the stacked lines and were assigned by position at 1000-2000 dpi. The kasratan under the ض of «بِأَرْضٍ» (b.14) sits beside «إِلَّا» on the next line and is not a fathatan on إلا. The stroke left of «عُرْضَتُهَا» (b.16) is the kasra under the hamza of «إِذَا» on the line above. The kasra of «عَرِقَتْ» is on the ra. The stroke above «إِذَا» (b.17b) is the kasra of «بِعَيْنَيْ». The double stroke above «الحِزَّانُ» is the kasratan of «لَهِقٍ». Marks deliberately not added, all confirmed at high zoom: ماءِ and سُعادُ (no fatha on mim/ain); مَحْنِيَة (final ta unvowelled); بأَبْطَحَ and بالْعَهْدِ (no kasra on ba); مِن دَمِهَا (no sukun on nun); مَوعُودَهَا (no sukun on waw); مُذَكَّرةٌ (no fatha on ra); مُقَلَّدُها and مُقَيَّدُها (ha unvowelled); بَناتِ (no fatha on nun); الغَرَابِيلُ، القَذَى، الغُيُوبَ، الحِزَّانُ، الأَعْلَامِ، الفَحْلِ، المَتْنَيْنِ (lam of the article without sukun, as printed). تَمَسَّكُ (b.10) shows two separate fathas, on the ta and on the mim. «كَمَا» in b.9 and b.10 both have fathas on the kaf and the mim. Bold: «دعها» is printed bold in all three places in gloss 12 (p.198). Its strokes are visibly thicker than the neighbouring «قال» and «حتىٰ», and the colon before it is regular. It is marked **دعها**. «في الحديث» on p.197 looks heavy, but its alif measures the same width as regular alifs (17 px at 1500 dpi), as do its dots (330 px), so it is not bold. The dark look of «جمع»، «بالحرف»، «الحركة»، «عظيمة» comes from the ligature glyphs. Dot-size and alif-width scans of all four gloss blocks found no other weight change. Quran: the two citations on p.200 (عبس 30، طه 118-119) are printed in the ordinary gloss naskh inside ornate brackets, not in the mushaf font. They are transcribed with exactly the printed marks (وَحَدَائِقَ without madda; تَظْمَأُ; ىٰ as drawn). The two ayahs of Taha are separated in print by a six-petal asterisk with no ayah numbers, written « * ». So scripts/quran.py may flag spelling differences from Tanzil. These are the book's own non-Uthmani spellings. Honorific: ﷺ glyph in gloss 6 (p.197) kept as U+FDFA. Process note: a project-wide grep run to look up the keyA ىٰ precedent also printed a few lines from keyB/b17.md and keyB/b27.md (pp.06x and 11x, unrelated to this batch). Nothing from keyB, diff, final or reports for pp.197-200 was opened.

keyB.notes: Batch b50 = pp.197-200 of قصيدة بانت سعاد (bayts 5-22), all in the stacked poetry layout; each page = :::شعر fence + :::مفردات glosses (+ :::حواشي variant footnotes on pp.198-199). p.196 ends with a complete bayt 4 and a gloss ending in a full stop, so p.197 takes a plain marker (no '+') and no (تابع). DAGGER ALIF: the gloss font draws a small dagger alif on every final ى (القذى، أضحى، الضحى، الأذى، حتى ×3، الذِّفَرى، يرى، تعالى، مثنى، عَلَى in the hadith), while the poem font never does; this is a glyph feature of that font (same as the automatic marks on الله, CONVENTIONS §2), so plain ى is written in ordinary text. Inside the Quran brackets on p.200 (تَعْرَىٰ، تَضْحَىٰ) the printed dagger is written as U+0670 per the §3 table (it matches the Uthmani text there). The hadith on p.197 («أَنَا فَرَطُكُمْ عَلَى الْحَوْضِ») is in the ordinary font without ﴿﴾ and is transcribed as ordinary vowelled text; ﷺ before it is the printed glyph. Gloss separators are the printed dashes, written as ASCII hyphen glued to the preceding word with a space after (مزجت- شَبِمٍ). Kashida inside stretched hemistichs (أَكْــرِمْ، الْحِـــزَّانُ, etc.) dropped. Footnote refs are glued inside the poetry lines (بِهَا(١)، فَلَا(١)، تُمْسِكُ(٢) on p.198; الْحِزَّانُ(١)، فَعْمٌ(٢) on p.199); validate.py only counts refs on prose lines, hence its two WARN lines 'footnote refs in text [] vs footnote lines [1, 2]' on pp.198-199 are expected and not a transcription gap. No [؟:…] markers were needed. validate.py printed OK.
